title: Balanced Triples and Global Crystal Bases

items.title: The bar lattice and the divided-power integral lattice of a based module
items.statement:
Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the two charts of $\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Z}$ over which the globalization is performed.

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ ($\lambda\in P^+$). Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$ (well defined because the highest vector is fixed). Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]; $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)$ are $\psi$-stable). Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$. The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; those are conclusions of the balanced-triple construction. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page.
items.strategy: A definition fixing the three lattices. The involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ maps $A_0$ isomorphically onto $A_\infty$, so $\psi(L)$ is an $A_\infty$-lattice generating $M$. $\psi(M_A)=M_A$ holds on $U_A$ by [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]], and $V_A(\lambda)$ is $\psi$-stable because $\psi(F_{i_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{i_k}^{(r_k)}v_\lambda)=F_{i_1}^{(r_1)}\cdots F_{i_k}^{(r_k)}v_\lambda$ on divided-power monomials. Nothing is asserted about $M_A\cap L$; in particular the definition hides no integral-freeness assumption and no self-duality of the lower lattice. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The integral residue lattices $L_A(\infty)$ and $L_A(\lambda)$
items.statement:
With $A,A_0,A_\infty,\psi$ as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]], fix $\lambda\in P^+$ and write $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Put $V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda\subseteq V(\lambda)$, the divided-power integral form of the simple integrable highest weight module; it is a $U_A$-submodule because $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ acts on the highest line through $U_A^+v_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$ and $U_A^0v_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$.

Define the **integral residue lattices**
$$L_A(\infty):=U_A^-\cap L(\infty),\qquad L_A(\lambda):=V_A(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda),$$
$A$-submodules of $U_q^-$ and $V(\lambda)$ respectively (intersections of the $A$-module $U_A^-$ resp. $V_A(\lambda)$ with the $A_0$-modules $L(\infty)$, $L(\lambda)$), together with the bar lattices $L(\infty)^-=\psi(L(\infty))$, $L(\lambda)^-=\psi(L(\lambda))$ and the balanced parts $E(\infty):=U_A^-\cap L(\infty)\cap L(\infty)^-$, $E(\lambda):=V_A(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)^-$.

The projection $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, restricts to the $A$-linear surjection $U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$; the **integral residue maps** are the canonical $A$-linear maps
$$L_A(\infty)\to L(\infty)/qL(\infty),\qquad L_A(\lambda)\to L(\lambda)/qL(\lambda).$$
This is the integral residue data of Kashiwara's §6.1. Only the containments and the $A$-linearity of $\pi_\lambda$ on the integral form are asserted: no freeness of $L_A(\infty)$ or $L_A(\lambda)$, no surjectivity or injectivity of the residue maps, no generation statement $U_A^-=A\cdot E(\infty)$ and no compatibility $\pi_\lambda(L_A(\infty))\subseteq L_A(\lambda)$ are asserted here; the last is a grand-loop consequence recorded later on this page.
items.strategy: Immediate from the definitions. $L_A(\infty)$ and $L_A(\lambda)$ are $A$-submodules because $U_A^-$, $V_A(\lambda)$ are $A$-modules and $L(\infty)$, $L(\lambda)$ are $A_0$-modules, hence $A$-modules. $\pi_\lambda(U_A^-)=V_A(\lambda)$ by definition of the latter. The residue maps are the composites with the quotient maps $L\mapsto L/qL$. The definition deliberately separates the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-lattices from the $A_0$- and $A_\infty$-lattices of the balanced triple; the residue and balancedness properties are proved in [[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]], [[lem-string-ideal-decomposition-of-the-integral-lattices]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]]. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Balanced triples over the two charts of $\mathbb P^1$ and the globalization map
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space, $V_A\subseteq V$ a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule with $\mathbb Q(q)V_A=V$ (not assumed free and not assumed to be an intersection of chart lattices), $L_0\subseteq V$ a free $A_0$-submodule with $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}L_0\to V$ an isomorphism, and $L_\infty\subseteq V$ a free $A_\infty$-submodule with $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_\infty}L_\infty\to V$ an isomorphism. This is the two-chart setting of $\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[q]\cup\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$ with the local rings $A_0=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}$ and $A_\infty=\mathbb Q[q^{-1}]_{(q^{-1})}$.

Put $E:=V_A\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ and define the **globalization map** $\varphi:E\to L_0/qL_0$, $e\mapsto e\bmod qL_0$. The triple $(V_A,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if $\varphi$ is an isomorphism. When it is, the inverse $G:L_0/qL_0\to E$ is the globalization map of the triple, and for every $\mathbb Q$-basis $B$ of $L_0/qL_0$ the family $G(B)$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $V$, an $A$-basis of $V_A$, an $A_0$-basis of $L_0$ and an $A_\infty$-basis of $L_\infty$; in particular balancedness implies that $V_A$ is free over $A$. In the applications of this page $V_A=M_A$, $L_0=L$ and $L_\infty=L^-$ come from [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]], and $B$ is the crystal basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ ([[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

$V_A$ is deliberately not assumed free: over the non-principal-ideal-domain ring $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ freeness is a conclusion of balancedness, not a hypothesis. The chart lattices $L_0$ and $L_\infty$ are free over the discrete valuation rings $A_0$ and $A_\infty$.
items.strategy:
The definition fixes the two-chart data. $\varphi$ is well defined because $E\subseteq L_0$. If the triple is balanced, the basis statements are formal from the inverse isomorphism together with the factorization isomorphisms $\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\to V_A\cap L_0$, $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\to V_A\cap L_\infty$, $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\to V_A$ of Kashiwara91 Lemma 7.1.1 ([[lem-balanced-triple-linear-algebra-over-the-projective-line]]); in the $A$-lattice case they are JKK Definition 8.1 and Theorem 8.2. The vector-bundle reading over the two affine charts is Kashiwara's remark after Lemma 7.1.2: a torsion-free coherent sheaf on $\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Z}$ is determined by its two chart restrictions, and balancedness says its global sections generate it. No choice principle is used in the definition.

Deliberate conventions: the condition is an isomorphism of $\varphi$ onto the $q=0$ residue, and the mirror condition onto the $q=\infty$ residue is equivalent ([[lem-balanced-triple-linear-algebra-over-the-projective-line]](iii)); the map is not assumed surjective onto $V_A$, and the lower integral lattice is not assumed to be its own form-dual. The crystal basis $B$ is a local basis at $q=0$; the global basis produced by $G$ is the *lower* global basis normalized by [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

items.title: The balanced-triple linear algebra over $\mathbb P^1$
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space, $M\subseteq V$ a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule with $\mathbb Q(q)M=V$, $L_0\subseteq V$ a free $A_0$-submodule with $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}L_0=V$, and $L_\infty\subseteq V$ a free $A_\infty$-submodule with $\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_\infty}L_\infty=V$. Put $E:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$.

(i) **Two-chart factorization (Kashiwara91 Lemma 7.1.1).** Assume $M\subseteq L_0\cap L_\infty$ and that the canonical map $E\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$ is an isomorphism. Then the canonical maps
$$\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\to M\cap L_0,\qquad \mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\to M\cap L_\infty,\qquad \mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\to M,\qquad E\to (M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
are isomorphisms, as are the base-change maps $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z[q]}(M\cap L_0)\to L_0$ and $A_\infty\otimes_{\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]}(M\cap L_\infty)\to L_\infty$. In particular $M\cap L_0$ is a free $\mathbb Z[q]$-module, $M\cap L_\infty$ is a free $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-module, and $M$ is a free $A$-module of rank $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V$; freeness is a conclusion, not a hypothesis.

(ii) **String-ideal step (Kashiwara91 Lemma 7.1.2).** Let $N\subseteq M$ be a sub-$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module and assume: (a) the canonical map $N\cap L_0\cap L_\infty\to(N\cap L_0)/(N\cap qL_0)$ is an isomorphism; (b) there exist a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ and a homomorphism $\phi:F\to M\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)$ with $M=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\phi(F)+N$ such that the two composites $F\to(L_0+\mathbb Z N)/(qL_0+\mathbb Z N)$ and $F\to(L_\infty+\mathbb Z N)/(q^{-1}L_\infty+\mathbb Z N)$ induced by $\phi$ are injective. Then $M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$ is an isomorphism, and
$$0\to (N\cap L_0)/(N\cap qL_0)\to (M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)\to (L_0+\mathbb Z N)/(qL_0+\mathbb Z N)\to 0$$
is exact, the image of the middle term being the $\mathbb Z$-span of the image of $\phi(F)$. One may take $F$ finitely generated, hence a free $\mathbb Z$-module.

(iii) **Free-lattice form (JKK Theorem 8.2, Lemma 8.4).** If $V_A$ is an $A$-lattice in $V$, then $(V_A,L_0,L_\infty)$ is balanced ([[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]]) if and only if $E\to L_0/qL_0$ is an isomorphism, if and only if $E\to L_\infty/q^{-1}L_\infty$ is an isomorphism; and if $F\subseteq E$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace such that $F\to L_0/qL_0$ and $F\to L_\infty/q^{-1}L_\infty$ are injective and $V_A=AF$, then $(V_A,L_0,L_\infty)$ is balanced and $F=E$.
items.strategy:
(i) Follow Kashiwara's proof. Set $E=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ and write $q^kE$ for the image of $E$ in $M$. The induction (7.1.1) gives $M\cap L_0\subseteq\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\mathbb Z q^kE+M\cap q^nL_0$ for every $n\ge1$: given $x\in M\cap L_0$, the hypothesis writes its class in $(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$ as the class of some $e\in E$, so $x-e\in M\cap qL_0$ and one iterates; the induction (7.1.2) then gives $(M\cap L_0)\cap q^nL_0=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\mathbb Z q^kE$. The first isomorphism follows by passing to the compatible system, and the $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$- and $A$-statements are its mirrors. The base-change statements are the vector-bundle translation: a torsion-free coherent sheaf on $\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Z}$ with global sections $E$ is generated by them, so its two chart restrictions are $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z[q]}(M\cap L_0)$ and $A_\infty\otimes_{\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]}(M\cap L_\infty)$, and the last displayed isomorphism of (i) is the statement that the global sections surject onto the $q=0$ fibre (the 'triviality of the vector bundle').

(ii) Replace $F$ by a finitely generated submodule of $\phi^{-1}(\dots)$ and $M$ by $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\phi(F')+N$, so that $F$ is free; since $\phi(F)\subseteq M\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)$ and $N\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)=N+M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, twist $\phi$ by a power of $q$ so that $\phi(F)\subseteq M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$. The two chart sequences of Lemma 7.1.1(i) for $N$ and for $M$ form a commutative ladder whose snake gives the exact sequence and the balancedness; applying (i) to $E'=\phi(F)\oplus(N\cap L_0\cap L_\infty)$ in place of $E$ gives the middle isomorphism.

(iii) JKK Theorem 8.2 is the equivalence in the free case; JKK Lemma 8.4 is the generation criterion quoted there from Kashiwara91 [10], and its proof is the argument of (i)–(ii) with the additional observation that $F\subseteq E\subseteq L_0\cap L_\infty$ already contains the $q=0$ and $q=\infty$ residues, so the two injectivity conditions are the balancedness isomorphisms.

All arguments are finite-dimensional linear algebra over the fields $\mathbb Q(q)$ and the residue fields, with the two discrete valuation rings $A_0$, $A_\infty$; the finite-dimensional hypothesis is applied componentwise to finite-dimensional graded pieces, which is legitimate because every vector has finite support. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Integral residues of the negative half: freeness, the crystal basis and the form characterization
items.strategy:
Kashiwara's Proposition 6.1.1 with its proof, in the library's normalizations. (iv) first: $\tilde f_i$ preserves $U_A^-$ by [[lem-divided-power-half-has-integral-skew-string-coefficients]] and preserves $L(\infty)$ by construction ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]]), so the $\tilde f$-monomials of $\mathbf 1$ lie in $L_A(\infty)$; their residue classes are the elements of $\mathcal B(\infty)$, which are $\mathbb Q$-linearly independent in $L(\infty)/qL(\infty)$ and generate it over $\mathbb Q$ ([[thm-crystal-basis-of-the-negative-half]]).

(i)–(ii): let $u=\sum_b a_b b\in L_A(\infty)/qL_A(\infty)$ with $a_b\in\mathbb Q$; for every $b'$, orthonormality of $\mathcal B(\infty)$ gives $a_{b'}=(u,b')_0$, and (iii) forces $(u,b')_0\in\mathbb Z$; hence $u$ is a $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of elements of $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and conversely every such combination lies in $L_A(\infty)/qL_A(\infty)$. This gives both the freeness and the characterization $\mathcal B(\infty)=\{u:(u,u)_0=1\}$ (the proof of Proposition 6.1.1(ii) shows that a nonzero $u$ with $(u,u)_0=1$ has exactly one nonzero coefficient and that coefficient $1$).

(iii): the exact denominator bound on $U_A^-$ is the form theorem, where divided-power words are word vectors divided by the Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$; the two normalizations (form and polarization) differ by the color-degree factor of the form theorem, which lies in $A$ after collecting $q$-powers, so $A_0$- and $A_{\mathrm{loc}}$-bounds intersect in $A_{\mathbb Z}$. The ring identity $A_0\cap A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A_{\mathbb Z}$ is immediate: an element of $A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with denominator a finite product of the $(1-q^{2n})$ is regular at $q=0$ iff its numerator lies in $\mathbb Z[q]$. Finally $A_{\mathbb Z}/qA_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z$ because $q\mapsto0$ kills the $q$-part and inverts each $1-q^{2n}$ to $1$.

The axiom of choice is inherited only through [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]] and through the generic-pairing/sparation supplier of the form theorem; the residue and integrality computations themselves are finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$ and choice-free.

items.title: Integrality of the string decomposition and the divided-power string ideals
items.statement:
Let $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$, and let $e_i',e_i''$ be the skew derivations of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]].

(i) **Integrality of the $i$-string components.** If $u\in U_A^-[-\nu]$ and $u=\sum_{l\ge0}F_i^{(l)}u_l$ is its $i$-string decomposition with $e_i'u_l=0$ for all $l$ ([[lem-divided-power-half-has-integral-skew-string-coefficients]]), then $u_l\in U_A^-[-\nu+l\alpha_i]$ for every $l$; equivalently $e_i'^{(n)}U_A^-\subseteq U_A^-$ for every $n\ge0$, where $e_i'^{(n)}=e_i'^n/[n]_i!$ is the divided skew derivation, and the projection $P_i=\sum_{l\ge0}(-1)^lq_i^{-l(l-1)/2}F_i^{(l)}e_i'^{(l)}$ onto $\ker e_i'$ along $F_iU_q^-$ preserves $U_A^-$. Here $F_i^{(l)}u_l$ with $u_l$ of the fixed weight has finite support in $l$ in each root degree.

(ii) **Divided-power string ideals.** With $(f_i^nU_q^-)_A:=f_i^nU_q^-\cap U_A^-$ and $(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A:=(f_i^nU_q^-)_A\,v_\lambda$, one has
$$(f_i^nU_q^-)_A=\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-,\qquad (f_i^nV(\lambda))_A=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda)=f_i^nV(\lambda)\cap V_A(\lambda),$$
the sums being finite in every root or label degree; in particular $(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A$ is a $U_A$-stable $A$-lattice of the $U_q$-submodule $f_i^nV(\lambda)$.

(iii) **Residue form of the string ideals.** For every $\alpha\in Q_+$ the canonical map
$$(f_i^nU_q^-)_A\cap L(\infty)\cap L(\infty)^-\longrightarrow\bigl((f_i^nU_q^-)_A\cap L(\infty)\bigr)\big/\bigl((f_i^nU_q^-)_A\cap qL(\infty)\bigr)$$
is an isomorphism onto $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Q b$. The analogous statement for the modules $f_i^nV(\lambda)$ is proved in [[lem-string-ideal-triples-are-balanced]] as the height-$r$ induction step.
items.strategy:
(i) The $i$-string decomposition and the projector are constructed in [[lem-divided-power-half-has-integral-skew-string-coefficients]], where it is proved that $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx$ lies in $U_A^-$; the commutation relation $(6.4)$ of the source (equivalently the first displayed commutation relation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]) shows that the set of $Q\in U_q^-$ with $e_i'^{(m)}Q\in U_A^-$ for all $m\ge0$ is stable under left multiplication by every $F_j^{(m)}$; hence $P_iU_A^-\subseteq U_A^-$ and the string components, read off from the projectors, are integral. This is Kashiwara's (6.1.2) and JKK's (10.1) with Lemma 10.1.

(ii) The inclusion $\supseteq$ is the definition. For the converse, the string decomposition expresses $u\in U_A^-\cap f_i^nU_q^-$ as $u=\sum_{l\ge0}F_i^{(l)}u_l$ with $u_l\in U_A^-$ by (i); since $u\in f_i^nU_q^-=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_q^-$ (a consequence of the string decomposition of the ambient field space) and the decomposition is unique, $u_l=0$ for $l<n$; this is $u\in\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-$. Applying $\pi_\lambda$ gives the module statement; the equality $(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A=f_i^nV(\lambda)\cap V_A(\lambda)$ follows because $f_i^nV(\lambda)\cap V_A(\lambda)\subseteq (f_i^nU_q^-)_Av_\lambda$ by the same string decomposition applied on the module side, using the module projector.

(iii) By (ii), $(f_i^nU_q^-)_A$ is the image of $\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-$; the $\tilde f$-monomial residues with $\tilde f_i^{\,n}$ acting nontrivially are exactly the images of the monomials of $B(\infty)_{-(\alpha-n\alpha_i)}$ under $\tilde f_i^{\,n}$, i.e. $B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}B(\infty)$; their classes are linearly independent and span the residue quotient by (i) and the crystal-limit axioms of [[thm-crystal-basis-of-the-negative-half]]. The argument is finite in each degree. For $\lambda\gg0$ this is the image of the same statement in $V(\lambda)$ under the field isomorphism $U_q^-[-\alpha]\to V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$; the module statement for general $\lambda$ is not asserted here. No new choice principle is used: the string decomposition is explicit and finite in each degree.

items.title: The string-ideal triples are balanced: the induction step (Kashiwara 7.4.1 / JKK 10.4)
items.statement:
Let $r\ge1$ and let $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$. Assume the following induction hypotheses in all degrees $\beta$ with $\operatorname{ht}(\beta)<r$:
$X_{r-1}$: for every $\beta$ with $\operatorname{ht}(\beta)<r$ the triple $(U_A^-[-\beta],L(\infty)_{-\beta},L(\infty)^-_{-\beta})$ is balanced, with inverse lift $G_\infty:\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\beta}\to U_A^-\cap L(\infty)\cap L(\infty)^-$;
$Y_{r-1}$: for every $\lambda\in P^+$ and every such $\beta$ the triple $(V_A(\lambda)_{\lambda-\beta},L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\beta},L(\lambda)^-_{\lambda-\beta})$ is balanced, with inverse lift $G_\lambda$;
$Z_{r-1}$: for every such $\beta$, every $\lambda$, every $i$ and every $n\ge0$, if $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\beta}\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}\mathcal B(\lambda)$ then $G_\lambda(b)\in(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A$.

Then for every $i\in I$, every $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, every $n\ge1$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$ the string-ideal triples
$$\Bigl((f_i^nV(\lambda))_A\cap L(\lambda),\ f_i^nV(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda),\ f_i^nV(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)^-\Bigr),\qquad \Bigl((f_i^nU_q^-)_A\cap L(\infty),\ f_i^nU_q^-\cap L(\infty),\ f_i^nU_q^-\cap L(\infty)^-\Bigr)$$
are balanced in degrees $\lambda-\alpha$ resp. $-\alpha$, and
$$(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A\cap L(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)^-\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}\mathcal B(\lambda)}\mathbb Q b,$$
with the corresponding display for $(f_i^nU_q^-)_A$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}\mathcal B(\infty)$.
items.strategy:
This is Kashiwara's Proposition 7.4.1 with its proof (JKK Proposition 10.4 in the $\mathbb Q[q,q^{-1}]$ form; for $a_{ii}=2$, the case of this library, JKK refer to Kashiwara91 [10]) together with Corollary 7.4.2/Corollary 10.6 for the negative half.

Module case. Descend on $n$. For $n$ larger than the length of $\alpha$ the claim is trivial. Assume it for $n+1$ (equation (7.4.2)). By [[lem-string-ideal-decomposition-of-the-integral-lattices]](ii), $(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda)$; for $l>n$, $l-1\ge n$ and $Z_{r-1}$ applied in the lower degree writes $F_i^{(l)}G_\lambda(b)=F_i^{(l-1)}G_\lambda(\tilde f_ib)$; more precisely $F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda)=F_i^{(n+1)}F_i^{(l-n-1)}V_A(\lambda)$ contributes to $(f_i^{n+1}V(\lambda))_A$, and the remaining $F_i^{(n)}V_A(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+n\alpha_i}$ is spanned over $A$ by the images $F_i^{(n)}G_\lambda(b)$ with $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+n\alpha_i}$. Splitting $b$ according to $\tilde e_ib=0$ or $\ne0$ and using $Z_{r-1}$ and the lower-degree balancedness puts $F_i^{(n)}G_\lambda(b)$ into $(f_i^{n+1}V(\lambda))_A$ when $\tilde e_ib\ne0$; hence $(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A=AF+V_n^{A,+1}$ with $F=\sum_{\tilde e_ib=0}\mathbb Q F_i^{(n)}G_\lambda(b)+E_{n+1}$ (equation (10.2) of JKK). The congruence $F_i^{(n)}G_\lambda(b)\equiv\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\bmod qL(\lambda)$ holds by [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]](b) iterated, and the two morphisms $F\to L_n/qL_n$ and $F\to L_n^-/q^{-1}L_n^-$ are isomorphisms by the residue form (iii) of [[lem-string-ideal-decomposition-of-the-integral-lattices]] and its $q=\infty$ mirror. Lemma 7.1.2/[[lem-balanced-triple-linear-algebra-over-the-projective-line]](ii) with $M=(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A\cap V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $N=(f_i^{n+1}V(\lambda))_A\cap V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and the displayed $F$ now gives the balancedness and the residue display.

Negative half. Corollary 7.4.2/[[lem-string-ideal-decomposition-of-the-integral-lattices]](iii) transfers the module statement to $U_q^-$ by taking $\lambda\gg0$ large in the regularized realization, where $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-[-\alpha]\to V(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is an isomorphism carrying $L(\infty)$, $L(\infty)^-$, $(f_i^nU_q^-)_A$ onto their module counterparts and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto the surviving subset of $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ ([[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]](a),(c),(d)); the finite degree statement is then transported back verbatim.

The axiom of choice is inherited only through the grand loop and the projection lemma named in the hypotheses, exactly as recorded there (clause J/N via the generic pairing comparison); the string computations themselves are finite per degree.

items.title: The highest weight and negative half integral crystal triples are balanced
items.statement:
Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, let $A_0,A_\infty,\psi$ be as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]], and let $L(\infty),L(\lambda)$ and $\mathcal B(\infty),\mathcal B(\lambda)$ be the Kashiwara lattices and crystal bases of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]] and [[thm-crystal-basis-of-the-negative-half]].

(i) **Negative half.** The triple $(U_A^-,L(\infty),L(\infty)^-)$ is balanced ([[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]]): the canonical map
$$E(\infty)=U_A^-\cap L(\infty)\cap L(\infty)^-\longrightarrow L(\infty)/qL(\infty)$$
is an isomorphism. Writing $G_\infty$ for its inverse, one has $G_\infty(b)\equiv b\bmod qL(\infty)$, and
$$U_A^-=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}A\,G_\infty(b),$$
a direct sum of free $A$-modules whose root-graded components have ranks $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\alpha]$. Moreover for every $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$
$$(f_i^nU_q^-)_A=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}\mathcal B(\infty)}A\,G_\infty(b).$$

(ii) **Highest weight modules.** For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the triple $(V_A(\lambda),L(\lambda),L(\lambda)^-)$ is balanced; writing $G_\lambda$ for the inverse of $E(\lambda)\to L(\lambda)/qL(\lambda)$ one has $G_\lambda(b)\equiv b\bmod qL(\lambda)$, and for every $i,n$
$$(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}\mathcal B(\lambda)}A\,G_\lambda(b).$$

(iii) **Projection and vanishing.** For every $\lambda\in P^+$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)$: if $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$ in $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ then $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda=0$, and if $\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0$ then $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$.

All assertions are componentwise in the finite-dimensional root/label components. In particular $U_A^-$ and each $V_A(\lambda)$ are free over $A$, and the divided-power halves have the classical PBW ranks. No integral freeness is assumed in the proof.
items.strategy:
Run Kashiwara's §§7.2–7.5 in the integral $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ form, in the same shape as the rational proof of JKK §10 (which is stated over $A=\mathbb Q[q,q^{-1}]$; the only difference is that the final linear-algebra step uses the non-free version of the chart lemma).

Induction statements, for $r\ge0$: $X(r)$ — for every $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ the negative-half triple $(U_A^-[-\alpha],L(\infty)_{-\alpha},L(\infty)^-_{-\alpha})$ is balanced; $Y(r)$ — for every $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $\lambda\in P^+$ the triple $(V_A(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha},L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha},L(\lambda)^-_{\lambda-\alpha})$ is balanced; $Z(r)$ — for every such degree the inverse lift $G_\lambda$ satisfies $G_\lambda(b)\in(f_i^nV(\lambda))_A$ whenever $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

Base: $r=0$. $L(\infty)_0=A_0\mathbf 1$, $L(\infty)^-_0=A_\infty\mathbf 1$, $U_A^-[0]=A\mathbf 1$; $L(\lambda)_\lambda=A_0v_\lambda$, $L(\lambda)^-_\lambda=A_\infty v_\lambda$, $V_A(\lambda)_\lambda=Av_\lambda$; the three display maps are the identity on $\mathbb Q\mathbf 1$ resp. $\mathbb Q v_\lambda$ (Kashiwara (7.5.4) at degree $0$).

Step: assume $X(r-1),Y(r-1),Z(r-1)$ and fix $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$. (a) The string-ideal step [[lem-string-ideal-triples-are-balanced]] gives, for every $i$ and $n\ge1$, the balancedness of $((f_i^nU_q^-)_A,L(\infty)\cap f_i^nU_q^-,L(\infty)^-\cap f_i^nU_q^-)$ and its module analogue in degree $\lambda-\alpha$, together with the residue displays. (b) Consequently each $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\cap\tilde f_i^{\,n}\mathcal B(\infty)$ carries the inverse lift $G_i$ of its string ideal, and Kashiwara's Lemma 7.5.1/JKK Lemma 10.7 — proved by testing against an auxiliary dominant weight with $\lambda(h_k)=0$ and $\lambda(h_p)\gg0$ for $p\ne k$ and reducing to the string-ideal balance — shows that $G_i(b)=G_j(b)$ for $b$ in the intersection of the two string ideals. Since every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\alpha\ne0$ satisfies $\tilde e_ib\ne0$ for some $i$ (the grand loop's finite-string endpoints), the map $G_\infty$ is well defined on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ by $G_\infty(b)=G_i(b)$ for any such $i$. (c) Setting $E=\sum_b\mathbb Z G_\infty(b)$ and $F=\mathbb Q E=\sum_b\mathbb Q G_\infty(b)\subseteq U_A^-\cap L(\infty)\cap L(\infty)^-$, the string decomposition gives $U_A^-=\sum_i(f_iU_q^-)_A$ and hence $U_A^-=A E$; the map $F\to L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/qL(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is an isomorphism onto the span of the $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ (by the string-ideal displays and the fact that every nonzero class in the crystal limit has a nonzero raising edge — the partial-inverse axiom of the crystal basis), and its $q=\infty$ mirror holds by applying $\psi$, which carries the $q=0$ chart into the $q=\infty$ chart and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto the corresponding bar basis. Lemma 7.1.1(iii)/[[lem-balanced-triple-linear-algebra-over-the-projective-line]] then gives $X(r)$: the triple is balanced and (7.5.5) holds in degree $-\alpha$. (d) For $Y(r)$ apply the same argument to the image under $\pi_\lambda$: the $\mathbb Q$-span $F_\lambda=\sum_{\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0}\mathbb Q G_\infty(b)v_\lambda\subseteq V_A(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\cap L(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)^-$ satisfies $V_A(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=AF_\lambda$; the injectivity of $F_\lambda\to L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}/qL(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is the bijection of surviving residues (grand loop N(r)), and the $q=\infty$ mirror is its $\psi$-image. The vanishing clause is Lemma 7.5.2: if $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$ and $\tilde e_ib\ne0$, then $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda\in(f_iV(\lambda))_A\cap qL(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)^-=0$ by the string-ideal balancedness of step (a); then $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ whenever the image survives, by uniqueness of the lift in $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ modulo the balanced map. (e) $Z(r)$ is the string-ideal membership of (a)-(b).

This closes the induction for every $r$, giving (i)–(iii); the direct sums are the degreewise identifications, and freeness with the classical ranks is the conclusion that each $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ is the $A$-span of the corresponding global basis elements, with ranks computed by the grand loop's crystal-basis cardinalities.

The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] but is inherited only through the grand loop and the projection lemma (clause J(r) and N(r), whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the QG-1 generic pairing); the lattice, balancedness and freeness arguments are finite per degree and choice-free. The owner direction records this inheritance chain as the only AC use of this page's integral construction.

items.title: The lower global basis of $U_q^-$ and of a highest weight module
items.statement:
Let $G_\infty:L(\infty)/qL(\infty)\to E(\infty)$ and $G_\lambda:L(\lambda)/qL(\lambda)\to E(\lambda)$ be the inverses of the balanced-triple isomorphisms of [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]]. The **lower global bases** are
$$\mathbf G(\infty):=\{G_\infty(b):b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\},\qquad \mathbf G(\lambda):=\{G_\lambda(b):b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\},$$
each element being normalized by the membership $G(b)\in E=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and the congruence $G(b)\equiv b\bmod qL$.

Conventions frozen by this definition: (a) $L=L(\infty)$ or $L(\lambda)$ is the $q=0$ lattice and $L^-=\psi(L)$ the $q=\infty$ lattice, so the normalization is 'lower'; (b) the bar is the **semilinear** involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]] with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, acting on $V(\lambda)$ by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$; (c) the $*$-convention of Kashiwara's §1.3 (a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear antiautomorphism with $E_i^*=E_i$, $F_i^*=F_i$, $(q^h)^*=q^{-h}$) is a different involution and belongs to the upper (form-dual) basis defined later on this page; (d) the naming dictionary is: Kashiwara's lower global basis $G(\lambda)$/$\mathbf G(\infty)$, JKK's $G(\lambda)/G(\infty)$, Lusztig's canonical basis in symmetric type (the agreement theorem later on this page), Brundan's lower global crystal base; the upper/dual-canonical basis is not this family. No bar-invariance, no uniqueness and no dual-basis property is asserted by this definition (the uniqueness theorem follows later on this page).
items.strategy: A definition freezing the normalization against the two chart lattices. The maps $G_\infty,G_\lambda$ exist by [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]]; the congruence $G(b)\equiv b\bmod qL$ restates that the balanced isomorphism is the residue map. The distinction between $\psi$ and $*$ is essential: $\psi$ is the bar used to define $L^-$ and the tensor bar, while $*$ is the antiautomorphism under which the polarization pairing is symmetric (Kashiwara91 Proposition 5.2.1) and which underlies the upper basis. The same symbol $G$ is used for both the negative half and the modules; consumers must keep the ambient lattice explicit. No choice principle is used in the definition.

items.title: Bar invariance, congruence and uniqueness of the lower global basis
items.statement:
Let $\psi$ be the bar involution and $\mathbf G(\infty),\mathbf G(\lambda)$ the lower global bases of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

(i) **Negative half.** For every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)$, $G_\infty(b)$ is the unique element $u\in U_A^-\cap L(\infty)$ with
$$u\equiv b\bmod qL(\infty),\qquad \psi(u)=u .$$

(ii) **Highest weight modules.** For every $\lambda\in P^+$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)$, $G_\lambda(b)$ is the unique element $u\in V_A(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)$ with
$$u\equiv b\bmod qL(\lambda),\qquad \psi(u)=u .$$

(iii) **Bases and freeness.** $\mathbf G(\infty)$ is an $A$-basis of $U_A^-$, an $A_0$-basis of $L(\infty)$, a $\mathbb Z[q]$-basis of $U_A^-\cap L(\infty)$ and a $\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $U_q^-$; $\mathbf G(\lambda)$ is an $A$-basis of $V_A(\lambda)$, an $A_0$-basis of $L(\lambda)$, a $\mathbb Z[q]$-basis of $V_A(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)$ and a $\mathbb Q(q)$-basis of $V(\lambda)$. The divided-power halves $U_A^\pm$ and every $V_A(\lambda)$ are therefore free over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$.
items.strategy:
Kashiwara's Theorem 7 with the proof of JKK Theorem 9.3, transferred to $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$.

Bar invariance. For $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)$ put $v:=(G_\lambda(b)-\psi(G_\lambda(b)))/(q-q^{-1})$. Write $G_\lambda(b)=\sum_jc_j(q)P_jv_\lambda$ with $c_j\in A$ and $P_j$ a divided-power monomial; this is possible because $G_\lambda(b)\in V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$. Then $\psi(G_\lambda(b))=\sum_jc_j(q^{-1})P_jv_\lambda$ and $v=\sum_j\frac{c_j(q)-c_j(q^{-1})}{q-q^{-1}}P_jv_\lambda\in V_A(\lambda)$, because divided differences of Laurent polynomials lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: for $c_j=q^n$, $\frac{q^n-q^{-n}}{q-q^{-1}}=q^{-n+1}(1+q^2+\cdots+q^{2n-2})\in A$. Moreover $v\in qL(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)^-$ because $\frac{1}{q-q^{-1}}=\frac{q}{q^2-1}\in qA_0\cap A_\infty$, and conjugation preserves $L(\lambda)$ (with $q\mapsto q^{-1}$) and hence maps $L(\lambda)$ to $L(\lambda)^-$. Thus $v\in E(\lambda)$ and $v\mapsto0$ in $L(\lambda)/qL(\lambda)$, so balancedness forces $v=0$, i.e. $\psi(G_\lambda(b))=G_\lambda(b)$. The same computation with $U_A^-\cap L(\infty)$ in place of $V_A(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)$ gives $\psi(G_\infty(b))=G_\infty(b)$.

Uniqueness. If $u\in V_A(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)$ satisfies $u\equiv b\bmod qL(\lambda)$ and $\psi(u)=u$, then $u\in L(\lambda)^-$ as well (since $u=\psi(u)\in\psi(L(\lambda))=L(\lambda)^-$), so $u\in E(\lambda)$ and $u-G_\lambda(b)$ has zero residue in $L(\lambda)/qL(\lambda)$; the balanced isomorphism is injective, hence $u=G_\lambda(b)$. The negative-half statement is identical with $U_A^-\cap L(\infty)$ in place of $V_A(\lambda)\cap L(\lambda)$.

Bases and freeness. In the balanced triple, $E=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ maps isomorphically onto $L/qL$; since $\{b\}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $L/qL$, $\{G(b)\}$ is a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $E$ and a fortiori $\mathbb Q$-independent; the factorization isomorphisms of the chart lemma give $M_A=A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E=\bigoplus_bA\,G(b)$, $L=A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E=\bigoplus_bA_0\,G(b)$ and $M_A\cap L=\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E=\bigoplus_b\mathbb Z[q]\,G(b)$. No choice principle beyond the inherited grand-loop comparison; the computation is finite per component.

items.title: The based quotient: projection of the lower global basis to a highest weight module
items.statement:
Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$.

(i) **Zero/survival.** For every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)$:
$$\pi_\lambda(b)=0\ \Longrightarrow\ G_\infty(b)v_\lambda=0,\qquad \pi_\lambda(b)\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ \pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b)).$$
Here $\pi_\lambda(b)$ is computed in the crystal limit: it is $0$ when the surviving-residue map kills $b$ ([[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]](c)).

(ii) **Lattice and operator compatibility.** $\pi_\lambda$ restricts to $A$-linear maps $L_A(\infty)\to L_A(\lambda)$ and $E(\infty)\to E(\lambda)$, the image $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal B(\infty))$ is $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and for all $P\in L(\infty)$ and $i\in I$,
$$\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda(P)\equiv\pi_\lambda(\tilde f_iP)\bmod qL(\lambda),\qquad \tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)\ \text{whenever }\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0 .$$

(iii) **Class form (based quotient).** In the $A$-bases of [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], the quotient map is the zero-or-basis-vector map
$$\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=\begin{cases}G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b)),&\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0,\\ 0,&\pi_\lambda(b)=0,\end{cases}$$
so the classes of the normalized negative-half basis elements map to one lower-global-basis class of $V_A(\lambda)$ or to zero. This is the based-quotient joint consumed by cyclotomic KLR categorification.
items.strategy:
Clauses (i) and (iii) restate [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]](iii) in the basis normalization of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]; the vanishing clause is Kashiwara's Lemma 7.5.2 (JKK's final step of $Y(r)$), which uses only the string-ideal balancedness of [[lem-string-ideal-triples-are-balanced]] and does not depend on the choice of the raising color.

Clause (ii): the residue-level statements are [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]](a)–(c), proved from the grand loop with the exact hypotheses: $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda(P)\equiv\pi_\lambda(\tilde f_iP)\bmod qL(\lambda)$ for $P\in L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ for surviving $b$. On the integral lattices: $\pi_\lambda(L_A(\infty))\subseteq L_A(\lambda)$ follows from the grand-loop lattice projection $\pi_\lambda(L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and $\pi_\lambda(U_A^-)\subseteq V_A(\lambda)$; the map on $E(\infty)$ lands in $E(\lambda)$ because $\pi_\lambda$ is $\psi$-equivariant on the divided-power forms ($\psi$ commutes with $\pi_\lambda$ since $\pi_\lambda(\psi(P))=\psi(P)v_\lambda=\psi(Pv_\lambda)$). Combining (i) with the residue congruences gives (iii). No premature statement is made for arbitrary integrable modules: the hypotheses are the grand loop's own, namely the chosen $P$-label grading, admissible finite string endpoints and the surviving-residue proviso; the operator congruences are asserted modulo $qL(\lambda)$ only.

The axiom of choice enters only through clauses (i) and (ii), i.e. through the grand loop's N(r) and the projection lemma, with the same inheritance as recorded there.

items.title: The upper (form-dual) global basis and the required perfectness of the integral pairing
items.statement:
Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)$, with balanced part $E=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and lower global basis $\mathbf G$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]; let $B$ be the normalized form of the library: the Lusztig–Kashiwara form on $U_q^-$ ([[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]) resp. the contravariant form on $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]), with its value at $q=0$ the orthonormal polarization ([[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]]).

The **form-dual (upper) lattice** inside $M$ is
$$E^\vee:=\{x\in M:\ B(x,E)\subseteq A\},$$
and the **upper global basis** $\{G^*(b)\}_{b\in\mathcal B}$ is the family determined by the two conditions
$$G^*(b)\in E^\vee,\qquad B(G(b'),G^*(b))=\delta_{bb'}\ \text{ for all }b'\in\mathcal B,$$
together with the upper congruence $G^*(b)\equiv b^*\bmod q^{-1}L^-$, where $b\mapsto b^*$ is the correspondence between the $q=0$ and $q=\infty$ crystal bases fixed by the two chart lattices.

This definition asserts none of the following: that $E^\vee$ is an $A$-lattice; that $E\subseteq E^\vee$ or $E^\vee\subseteq L^-$; that the family $\{G^*(b)\}$ exists, is an $A$-basis of $E^\vee$, or is dual to $\mathbf G$; or that the lower integral lattice is self-dual over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. These are exactly the claims requiring proof, collected as the **perfectness assertion of the integral pairing**:
$$E^\vee\ \text{is a free }A\text{-module},\quad B:E^\vee\times E\to A\ \text{is perfect},\quad \{G^*(b)\}\ \text{is the dual }A\text{-basis},$$
together with the crystal compatibility of the two bases. They are proved in the next item. The upper lattice is a *form-dual*, not the bar lattice $L^-$ of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]], and not the lower lattice under an automatic self-duality.
items.strategy: A definition with its required-perfectness clause stated explicitly, so that no consumer can read the upper basis as a formal dual without proof. The normalization of $B$ is the one whose $q=0$ reduction is the orthonormal polarization of [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]]; the two normalizations of the half form (the divided-power norm of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and the polarization norm) differ by the color-degree factor recorded there, and the strategy of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]] must pin the dictionary before any dual basis is formed. The existence of $E^\vee$ as an $A$-module and the non-triviality of the self-duality question are visible already in rank one, where the divided-power norms are $1/[a]_{q^2}!$ and the dual of the lower lattice is not the lower lattice in the unnormalized pairing. No choice principle is used in the definition.

items.title: Upper and lower global bases are dual and crystal compatible
items.statement:
Retain the notation of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]].

(i) **Perfectness.** The form-dual $E^\vee$ is a free $A$-module, the pairing $B:E^\vee\times E\to A$ is $A$-bilinear and perfect (the inclusion $E\subseteq E^\vee$ is not asserted; the lower lattice and its form-dual may differ), and the family $\{G^*(b)\}$ is an $A$-basis of $E^\vee$ dual to the lower global basis: $B(G(b'),G^*(b))=\delta_{bb'}$.

(ii) **Crystal compatibility.** The residue classes of $\{G^*(b)\}$ form the upper crystal basis: under the identification $E^\vee/...$ the classes of $G^*(b)$ are the elements $b^*$ of the $q=\infty$ crystal basis, and for every $i$ the adjunction formulas
$$B(\tilde f_iu,v)=B(u,\tilde e_iv),\qquad B(\tilde e_iu,v)=B(u,\tilde f_iv)$$
hold on the appropriate components of $U_q^-$ and of the $V(\lambda)$, in the exact normalization pinned in the proof; equivalently $\tilde e_i$ is the $B$-adjoint of $\tilde f_i$.

(iii) **Non-self-duality guard.** The theorem does not assert $E^\vee=E$, nor $\{G^*(b)\}=\{\pm G(b)\}$; in rank one the exact index of $E$ in $E^\vee$ is computed in the companion example, and the identification $\{G^*(b)\}=\{\pm G(b)\}$ in general type is a strict additional statement, proved only in symmetric type (the agreement theorem later on this page).

items.title: Lusztig's canonical basis and Kashiwara's lower global basis agree in symmetric type
items.statement:
Assume the Cartan datum is symmetric of finite type $A_n,D_n,E_6,E_7,E_8$ (all $d_i=1$ and the Cartan matrix symmetric), over the rational function field $\mathbb Q(q)$, with the library's Chevalley generators $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ and the bar involution $\psi$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

(i) The dictionary: identify the negative half $U_q^-$ used here with the algebra $\mathbf f$ of Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis by the identity on the divided-power generators $F_i^{(n)}$; identify the bar involutions ($\psi$ here, $\bar{\ }$ there) by $\psi(F_i^{(n)})=F_i^{(n)}$; identify the bilinear forms by the normalization of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] against Lusztig's form of Ch. 1.2 and Ch. 14.4; identify the $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-forms by $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-span of the divided powers.

(ii) Under this dictionary the lower global basis $\mathbf G(\infty)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] equals Lusztig's canonical basis of $\mathbf f$, and, for every $\lambda\in P^+$, the lower global basis $\mathbf G(\lambda)$ of $V(\lambda)$ equals the canonical basis of the integrable highest weight module transported through the same dictionary.

(iii) The theorem is the identification of two constructions, not of two names: each clause of the dictionary (integral form, bar, form, generator normalization) must be checked separately, and the identification is asserted only in symmetric type. In non-symmetric type the corresponding identification of the upper basis with Lusztig's dual canonical basis is not asserted.
items.strategy: Intended route (owner-held on the source side). Kashiwara's introduction states the agreement in $A_n,D_n,E_n$ and attributes the canonical-basis side to Lusztig's series; the proof strategy is to match, one by one, the four items of the dictionary and then invoke the uniqueness characterization of both bases: (a) the integral form: Lusztig's $\mathcal A$-form of $\mathbf f$ is generated by the divided powers (Lusztig Ch. 14.4, or Ch. 23.2 after the change of rings), matching [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]; (b) the bar: both are the unique semilinear involution fixing the generators and inverting $q$, matching [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]; (c) the form: Lusztig's symmetric bilinear form on $\mathbf f$ has the same normalization on divided powers as the form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], after the color-degree factor; (d) uniqueness: a subset of $\mathbf f$ that is bar-invariant, contains the crystal limit classes and is unitriangular with respect to the word basis is unique (both constructions characterize their basis this way). items.title: Specialization of the global bases and the root-of-unity boundary
items.statement:
Let $\lambda\in P^+$.

(i) **Characteristic-zero $q=1$ specialization.** For every characteristic-zero field $k$, the fibre $V_A(\lambda)\otimes_Ak$ under $q\mapsto1$ is a free $k$-module with basis the images of the lower global basis $\mathbf G(\lambda)$, its weight dimensions are $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu$, and it is the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the explicitly regularized realization; thus the character of $V(\lambda)$ is the Weyl–Kac character (the finite Weyl character in finite type). The specialization is computed in the positive toral quotient $k[H_i]$ of [[prop-specialization-at-q-one-recovers-the-classical-enveloping-relations]] and [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]; no direct substitution in rational quantum denominators is used.

(ii) **Which specializations preserve a basis.** The global basis survives every flat base change $A\to A'$ that is injective with $A'\otimes_A\bigoplus_bA\,G(b)$ identified with $\bigoplus_bA'G(b)$: in particular the localizations at $q=1$, at $q=0$ (giving $L(\lambda)$) and at $q=\infty$ (giving $L(\lambda)^-$), and residue-field specializations at $q=\zeta$ with $\zeta$ not a root of unity.

(iii) **Root-of-unity boundary.** At a root of unity $\zeta$, the divided-power form $U_A$ does not specialize to the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra: the Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$ are not units at $\zeta$, the divided powers are not generated by the ordinary generators, and the specialization may lose semisimplicity; the global basis of this page is not asserted to specialize to a basis of an integrable highest weight module over $\mathbb Z[q]/(\Phi_m)$ at a root of unity.
items.strategy:
(i) The global basis is an $A$-basis of $V_A(\lambda)$ ([[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]), so its image is a spanning set of the fibre; base change of the finite free weight components preserves dimensions, and the computed fibre is identified with the classical simple integrable highest module by the local $q=1$ deformation theorem ([[lem-local-q-one-deformation-proves-integrable-highest-weight-universality]]) and the specialization proposition. Surjectivity onto the classical module and equality of dimensions make the images a basis. Weyl–Kac then gives the character. The passage to the positive toral quotient is the one supplied by [[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]]; no denominator is specialized.

(ii) Flat base change preserves direct sums and the basis property; the $q=0$ and $q=\infty$ instances are the two chart identifications of the balanced triple, and a non-root-of-unity residue field keeps every $[r]_{q_i^2}!$ invertible, so the integral form and the basis persist.

(iii) At a root of unity the denominator $[r]_{q_i^2}!$ is divisible by the cyclotomic polynomial defining the fibre, so the inclusion $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\to$ the local ring is not the right place to specialize the divided powers; the known failure of semisimplicity shows that no basis statement of this type may be transported. No assertion is made. No new choice principle is used.

items.title: Integral triangular decomposition and freeness of the Lusztig form
items.statement: Assume AC only for the generic/classical PBW rank supplier. Over A=Z[q,q^-1], multiplication U_A^-⊗_A U_A^0⊗_A U_A^+→U_A is an isomorphism. The two divided-power halves are free A-modules with finite free root components of the classical PBW ranks. The unmodified torus has an A-basis K_c∏K_i^{delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}, with delta_i=0 or1 and c representing Pvee/Σ Z(d_i h_i). Hence U_A is free, and the degree-beta component is ⊕_{alpha,gamma∈Q_+, alpha-gamma=beta} U_A^-[-gamma]⊗U_A^0⊗U_A^+[alpha]. Unique coefficients refer to products of chosen basis elements, not to arbitrary sums of simple tensors.

That construction starts with an arbitrary Z[q±]-submodule and rational DVR-free chart lattices; its integral residue and height/string-ideal argument proves the actual A-basis as a conclusion. Use its negative-half global basis in each finite root degree. The unmodified integral toral-basis lemma independently supplies the full K_coset ∏K_i^delta_iT_{i,0,t_i} A-basis by Gaussian Vandermonde, toral shift/action recursions and Laurent-extremal independence. Both factors are genuinely free over the non-PID A; their tensor product with the positive half is free. Reordering gives the multiplication surjection; tensoring a kernel with Q(q) gives zero by field triangular decomposition, and the free source has no torsion, so the kernel is zero. Its homogeneous restriction gives the negative-toral-positive root decomposition. Extension to Q(q) and the published generic/classical comparison give the claimed component ranks, with AC used only in that rank supplier. No torsionfree-to-free claim over A and no modified dot-U basis is used.

items.title: Finitely generated free integral weight lattices and deformation of the classical weight character
items.statement: For every dominant label weight lambda, let V_A=U_Av_lambda=U_A^-v_lambda inside the simple integrable L(lambda). Over A=Z[q,q^-1], each label-weight component of V_A is finite FREE of rank dim_Q(q)L(lambda)_mu, not merely torsionfree. It spans the field module. For every characteristic-zero q=1 specialization k, the fibre has the same weight dimensions and is the classical simple integrable highest module of the explicitly regularized realization, transported to the original label lattice. Thus its character is the Weyl-Kac character (the finite Weyl character in finite type). The integral Serre quotient equals L(lambda) in every symmetrizable type, as already proved by the early local comparison.
items.strategy: The simultaneous global construction and its based-quotient theorem give a Z[q±]-basis of U_A^-v_lambda: each negative global basis element maps to the corresponding highest-module global element if its crystal image survives, and to0 otherwise (Kashiwara91 Theorem7(ii), Section7.5.2). Thus each finite weight lattice is actually free over A, with rank its field dimension. The early local-q1 deformation/universality theorem already proves the simple quantum module, field character and equality with the integrable Serre quotient using DVR-free lattices; it is not dependent on this global result. Base change of the newly proved integral weight basis preserves dimensions. Algebraic positive specialization and finite-support regularization identify the classical fibre and its character, and the classical Weyl-Kac theorem gives the explicit formula. items.title: The root-height completion for weightwise quasi-$R$ intertwiners
items.statement:
Let $U_q=U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its positive and negative halves $U_q^\pm$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]) and let $Q_+$ be the positive root lattice. Consider the direct product
$$\prod_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\beta]\otimes U_q^+[\beta],$$
regarded as a module of operators on tensor products $M\otimes N$ whose weight components are finite-dimensional and bounded above: an element $\Theta=(\Theta_\beta)_\beta$ acts on a tensor vector $m\otimes n$ by the sum $\sum_\beta\Theta_\beta(m\otimes n)$ whenever that sum is finite. The completion is the one determined by the descending filtration by $\operatorname{ht}(\beta)\ge N$ (the analogue of the completion $D_q(\mathfrak g)\hat\otimes D_q(\mathfrak g)$ of the Drinfeld double); on every finite-dimensional weight component of $M\otimes N$ the filtration is eventually constant, so the sum is defined there.

This is **not** a universal $R$-matrix and **not** a quasitriangular Hopf structure on $U_q$: no invertibility, no Yang–Baxter equation and no braiding is asserted. Only the weightwise-finite evaluation on tensor vectors of bounded-above support is defined. $\Theta_0=1\otimes1$ is fixed; the tensor order is 'negative half first, positive half second', matching the pairing convention fixed later on this page and the tensor bar built from it.
items.strategy: A definition of the completion. The filtration degree is the height of the root; each finite-dimensional weight component of a tensor product of bounded-above modules meets only finitely many filtration layers, so an element of the product evaluates there. The phrase 'weightwise' is essential: without bounded-above support the sum need not converge, and no universal object is asserted. The negative-first order is fixed because the dual-basis tensors of [[lem-homogeneous-dual-basis-sums-are-basis-independent-and-weightwise-finite]] pair $U_q^-[-\beta]$ with $U_q^+[\beta]$ and the tensor bar of [[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]] acts on $M\otimes N$ by applying $\Theta$ after the bar. No choice principle is used in the definition.

items.title: The Drinfeld pairing between the positive and negative quantum halves
items.statement:
Let $\omega$ be the Chevalley involution of [[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], $\omega(E_i)=-F_i$, $\omega(F_i)=-E_i$, $\omega(K_h)=K_{-h}$, a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism with $\omega(U_q^+)=U_q^-$ and $\omega(U_q^-)=U_q^+$; let $B$ be the normalized Lusztig–Kashiwara form on the negative half ([[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]), homogeneous and with $B(1,1)=1$.

Define the **Drinfeld pairing** $(\ ,\ ):U_q^+\times U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ by
$$(x,y):=(-1)^{\operatorname{ht}(\beta)}B(\omega(x),y)\qquad(x\in U_q^+[\beta],\ y\in U_q^-).$$
Conventions fixed by this definition: (a) the sign $(-1)^{\operatorname{ht}(\beta)}$ is chosen so that $(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and $(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_i!$ for all $i,n\ge0$ (the values read off from $B(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})$ in the form theorem); equivalently $(E_i,F_i)=1$ rather than the shuffle normalization $(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$; (b) the pairing is $\mathbb Q(q)$-bilinear, homogeneous, and restricted to $U_q^\pm$ in each argument; (c) the coproduct used in the adjointness identities proved later on this page is the library's $\Delta$ with $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$ and $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]); this convention determines the coefficients and the tensor order of $\Theta$ in [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]]. No nondegeneracy, no integrality and no relation to $\Theta$ is asserted here.
items.strategy: The transport is well defined because $\omega$ maps $U_q^+[\beta]$ isomorphically onto $U_q^-[-\beta]$ and $B$ is defined on all of $U_q^-$. The sign is fixed by the displayed generator values: $B(\omega(E_i),F_i)=B(-F_i,F_i)=-B(F_i,F_i)=-1$ in the normalization of the form theorem ($B(F_i,F_i)=1$), so the sign-normalized pairing has $(E_i,F_i)=1$. The divided-power value follows from $B(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_i!$ and $\omega(E_i^{(n)})=(-1)^nF_i^{(n)}$, the sign being cancelled by the declared factor. The dictionary between this normalization and the formal shuffle pairing $(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ is the color-degree scaling recorded in the form theorem; it is part of the proof of the next item, not an assumption. No choice principle is used in the definition.

items.title: The Drinfeld pairing is nondegenerate in each root degree and matches the shuffle pairing
items.statement:
Let $(\ ,\ )$ be the pairing of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]]. Then:
(i) $(\ ,\ )$ is homogeneous: $(U_q^+[\beta],U_q^-[\gamma])=0$ unless $\beta=\gamma$; and it descends to the Serre quotients $U_q^+$ and $U_q^-$ on both sides (the form on the halves is defined on the actual quotients, not only on free words).
(ii) It is nondegenerate in each finite root degree: for every $\beta\in Q_+$ the restriction $(\ ,\ ):U_q^+[\beta]\times U_q^-[-\beta]\to\mathbb Q(q)$ is a perfect pairing of finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector spaces; equivalently the map $U_q^+[\beta]\to(U_q^-[-\beta])^*$ is an isomorphism.
(iii) Generator values and normalization:
$$(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij},\qquad (E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_i!\quad(n\ge0),$$
and $(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(m)})=0$ for $n\ne m$ in a fixed simple root direction; the divided-power normalizations are those of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]].
(iv) **Match with the shuffle pairing.** The pairing of (ii) agrees, up to the explicit color-degree factor of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with the restriction to the actual Serre quotients of the formal generic Hopf pairing of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]]; in particular its nondegeneracy is the descent of that generic pairing through the Serre ideals, and the coproduct-adjointness identities hold:
$$(xx',y)=\sum(x\otimes x',\Delta(y)),\qquad (x,yy')=\sum(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(x),y\otimes y'),$$
with the tensor factors paired against each other in the displayed orders.
items.strategy:
(i) Both $B$ and $\omega$ preserve the $Q$-grading (up to the sign $\omega$ changes the sign of the root degree), and $B$ is homogeneous and orthogonal on distinct degrees; hence the transported pairing is homogeneous. Descent to the Serre quotients is inherited: $B$ is defined on the actual quotient $U_q^-$ (its construction/homogeneity and the separation lemma prove that the recursively defined values kill the Serre ideal), and $\omega$ carries the positive Serre ideal to the negative one, so the transported pairing is well defined on $U_q^+\times U_q^-$.

(ii) $\omega$ is an algebra isomorphism $U_q^+[\beta]\to U_q^-[-\beta]$ of finite-dimensional spaces and the sign is a unit, so the pairing is perfect exactly when $B$ is nondegenerate on $U_q^-[-\beta]$, which is clause (iii) of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]].

(iii) Evaluated on generators, $(\omega(E_i),F_i)=B(-F_i,F_i)=-1$, so $(E_i,F_i)=1$; for the divided powers use the explicit rank-one values $B(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_i!$ of the form theorem and the sign cancellation. Distinct $n,m$ are separated by homogeneity in the root direction.

(iv) The form $B$ was constructed from the generic pairing by the separation lemma and the color-degree scaling recorded in the form theorem; transport by $\omega$ preserves that construction. The coproduct adjointness follows from the defining recursion $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$ of the negative-half form together with the Chevalley transport, or equivalently from the defining property of the generic half pairing; the tensor order displayed is the one induced by the library's coproduct of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]], and the author must verify the two scalar twists (the sign and the color-degree factor) against that item. The inherited Axiom-of-Choice use of the generic pairing supplier is recorded at [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]].

items.title: Homogeneous dual-basis sums: basis independence and weightwise finiteness
items.strategy:
(i) If $\{u'_j\}$ is another basis with dual $\{v'_j\}$ and $u'_j=\sum_i a_{ji}u_i$, then $v_i=\sum_j a_{ji}v'_j$, so $\sum_j u'_j\otimes v'_j=\sum_{ij}a_{ji}u_i\otimes v'_j=\sum_i u_i\otimes v_i$.

(ii) $\Theta_\beta$ maps $M_\mu\otimes N_\nu$ to $M_{\mu+\beta}\otimes N_{\nu-\beta}$. Since $\operatorname{wt}(M)$ is bounded above by some $\lambda$ and has finite-dimensional weight components, the set of $\beta\in Q_+$ with $\mu+\beta\in\operatorname{wt}(M)$ and $\nu-\beta\in\operatorname{wt}(N)$ is finite: $\beta$ is determined by the weight $\mu+\beta$ of $M$, and only finitely many weights of $M$ lie above $\mu$. For finite-degree polynomial type-A modules the same bounded-above argument applies (their weights lie in a finite set). Hence the sum is finite on every tensor vector.

(iii) The same counting with $\operatorname{ht}(\beta)\ge N_0$: the contributing $\beta$ form a subset of the finite set of (ii). No choice principle: the dual basis is unique once a basis is chosen, and the independence clause removes the choice. Note that (i)–(iii) do not require the modules to be based; only integrability, finiteness of weight components and bounded-above support are used.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the weightwise quasi-$R$ intertwiner
items.statement:
Let $\Theta=(\Theta_\beta)_\beta\in\prod_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\beta]\otimes U_q^+[\beta]$ be the family of homogeneous dual-basis tensors of [[lem-homogeneous-dual-basis-sums-are-basis-independent-and-weightwise-finite]], with $\Theta_0=1\otimes1$, and let $\Psi$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism of the completed tensor square determined on generators by
$$\Psi(K_h\otimes1)=K_h\otimes1,\quad \Psi(1\otimes K_h)=1\otimes K_h,\quad \Psi(E_i\otimes1)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1},\quad \Psi(1\otimes E_i)=K_i^{-1}\otimes E_i,\quad \Psi(F_i\otimes1)=F_i\otimes K_i,\quad \Psi(1\otimes F_i)=K_i\otimes F_i .$$
Then:
(i) **Intertwining.** For every $u\in U_q=\mathbb Q(q)\langle E_i,F_i,K_h^{\pm1}\rangle$ one has, in the completion,
$$\Theta\,\Delta(u)=\bigl(\Psi\circ\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\bigr)(u)\,\Theta,$$
where $\Delta$ is the library coproduct $\Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i$, $\Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i$ ([[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]). Equivalently the homogeneous components satisfy the four degree-by-degree recursions
$$\Theta_\beta(1\otimes E_i)+\Theta_{\beta-\alpha_i}(E_i\otimes K_i)=\Psi(E_i\otimes1)\Theta_{\beta-\alpha_i}+\Psi(K_i\otimes E_i)\Theta_\beta,$$
$$\Theta_\beta(F_i\otimes1)+\Theta_{\beta-\alpha_i}(K_i^{-1}\otimes F_i)=\Psi(1\otimes F_i)\Theta_{\beta-\alpha_i}+\Psi(F_i\otimes K_i^{-1})\Theta_\beta,$$
together with the two toral equations $\Theta_\beta(K_h\otimes K_h)=\Psi(K_h\otimes K_h)\Theta_\beta$.
(ii) **Uniqueness.** $\Theta$ is the unique element of the completion with $\Theta_0=1\otimes1$ satisfying (i); each $\Theta_\beta$ is determined by the lower components through the degree-$\beta$ recursion.
(iii) **Evaluability.** $\Theta$ acts on every finite tensor product of modules with finite-dimensional weight components and bounded-above weight support ([[lem-homogeneous-dual-basis-sums-are-basis-independent-and-weightwise-finite]]); the construction is at the field level $\mathbb Q(q)$ and makes no integrality claim: the divided-power integrality of the action on based lattices is a separate, later item on this page.
items.strategy:
Adapt Lacabanne's proof of Proposition 1.14 (which follows Jantzen Ch. 7 Lemma 7.1) to the library's coproduct and pairing conventions, with the dictionary verified as follows: (a) the pairing is the transported negative-half form of [[lem-the-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-is-nondegenerate-in-each-root-degree]], whose generator values $(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ fix the scalar twists; (b) the commutation identity for a homogeneous $x\in U_q^+[\beta]$ and the generators, $xF_i-F_ix=(K_ir_i(x)-r_i'(x)K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ and its mirror for $E_i$, is the same calculation as in the source (Lemma 1.6), and follows here from the defining recursion $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$ of the negative-half form together with the Chevalley transport; (c) expanding the two sides of the $\beta$-component equation and using the basis expansions $x=\sum_i(x,v_i)u_i$, $y=\sum_i(u_i,y)v_i$ of the dual-basis lemma reduces each recursion to the commutation identity.

Existence: the toral equations hold because $\Theta_\beta$ is a weight-zero tensor and $K$'s are grouplike; the two $E$- and $F$-recursions are solved degree by degree for $\Theta_\beta$ from the already constructed $\Theta_{\beta-\alpha_i}$; this is exactly the source's computation, the displayed recursion is solved by applying the projectors onto the kernels of the adjoint $E_i$- and $F_i$-actions, and the two solutions agree by the Jacobi-type compatibility of the positive and negative recursions (the source proves both simultaneously and checks the generators $E_j,F_j,K_j$ of the second factor). Uniqueness: if $\Theta'$ is another solution, then $\delta=\Theta-\Theta'$ has $\delta_0=0$ and satisfies the homogeneous recursion $\delta_\beta(1\otimes E_i)+\delta_{\beta-\alpha_i}(E_i\otimes K_i)=\Psi(E_i\otimes1)\delta_{\beta-\alpha_i}+\Psi(K_i\otimes E_i)\delta_\beta$; the minimum-height nonzero component of $\delta$ is annihilated by the projectors and the recursion forces it to vanish, so $\delta=0$ by induction on height.

(iii) is the finiteness of the dual-basis lemma. The exact statement is field-level; no divided-power denominator is estimated here, and the integrality item is deliberately separate and scheduled after the integral bases, exactly as the owner direction prescribes. The dictionary obligation (the source's double $D_q(\mathfrak g)$ carries a doubled torus; only the $K$-toral part acts here, the difference being the scalar factor $K_\beta$ absorbed in the tensor order) is part of the proof: it must be checked on generators before the source's equations may be quoted.

items.title: Divided-power integrality of the quasi-$R$ action on based lattices
items.statement:
Let $M,N$ be based integrable modules in the finite-weight-space highest weight category $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{int}}$, with divided-power integral lattices $M_A,N_A$ and lower global bases $\mathbf G_M,\mathbf G_N$ ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]), or finite-degree polynomial type-A modules with their $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-lattices. Let $\Theta=(\Theta_\beta)$ be the weightwise quasi-$R$ intertwiner of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]].

(i) **Preservation of the integral tensor lattice.** $\Theta$ maps $M_A\otimes_AN_A$ into itself: for every $m\in M_A$, $n\in N_A$ the sum $\sum_\beta\Theta_\beta(m\otimes n)$ has only finitely many nonzero terms and lies in $M_A\otimes_AN_A$.
(ii) **Integral coefficients.** Expressing $m,n$ in the lower global bases and $\Theta_\beta$ in the divided-power tensor lattice $U_A^+[\beta]\otimes U_A^-[-\beta]$, the coefficients of $\Theta_\beta(m\otimes n)$ are in $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$; equivalently, the sum of dual bases $\sum_i u_i\otimes v_i$ computed over an $A$-basis $\{u_i\}$ of $U_A^+[\beta]$ has dual basis $\{v_i\}\subseteq U_A^-[-\beta]$ after the normalization of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]].
(iii) **Triangularity.** The expansion of $\Theta(m\otimes n)$ in the tensor product of lower global bases is dominance-triangular with diagonal $1$: the leading term of the $\beta$-component on a tensor monomial is the monomial itself, and all other terms involve strictly smaller dominant exponents; consequently the tensor bar preserves the $A$-lattice even without assuming that the lower lattice is self-dual.

This is the divided-power integrality joint. It is **not** inferred from lattice freeness: clause (ii) is a coefficient computation in the divided-power pairing, and clause (iii) is a triangularity statement about the dual-basis sum.

items.title: The balanced triple and global basis for the two-dimensional $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-module
items.strategy:
Direct computation in the two-dimensional module.

(a) $U_A^-=\langle F_1\rangle_A$ acts on $V(\omega)$ by $F_1^{(n)}v=0$ for $n\ge2$, $F_1^{(n)}w=0$ for $n\ge1$, so $V_A(\omega)=Av\oplus Aw$. The Kashiwara lattice $L(\omega)=A_0v\oplus A_0w$ has crystal basis $\{v+qL,w+qL\}$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]); applying $\psi$ (which fixes $v$ and $w$) gives $L(\omega)^-=A_\infty v\oplus A_\infty w$. Intersecting the three lattices gives (a) because $A\cap A_0\cap A_\infty=\mathbb Z$ and $Av\oplus Aw=(A\cap A_0\cap A_\infty)\cdot(v,w)$.

(b) $\varphi:E\to L/qL$ sends $av+bw$ to $\bar a(v+qL)+\bar b(w+qL)$; since $B=\{v+qL,w+qL\}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis and $A/qA=\mathbb Z$ (via $q\mapsto0$), $\varphi$ identifies $E$ with the free $\mathbb Z$-module on $\{v+qL,w+qL\}$, hence is an isomorphism: this is the rank-one case of the chart lemma. The lower global basis is read off: $G(v+qL)=v$, $G(w+qL)=w$; bar-invariance is the computation $\psi(v)=v$ (from $\psi(v_\lambda)=v_\lambda$) and $\psi(w)=\psi(F_1)v=F_1v=w$.

(c) $f_1V(\omega)=Aw$ is one-dimensional and equals its own intersection with both chart lattices; the residue class of $w$ is the sole crystal element of that weight.

(d) The rank-one quasi-$R$ twist is $\Theta_{b}=1\otimes1$ and $\Theta_{b}\otimes\Theta_{b}=\bigl(1\otimes1\bigr)+c\,E\otimes F$ with the normalization $(E,F)=1$, i.e. $c=1$; acting on the four monomials, $E\otimes F$ kills $v\otimes w,v\otimes v$ and sends $w\otimes v\mapsto v\otimes v$, $w\otimes w\mapsto v\otimes w$, so $\Theta(w\otimes v)=w\otimes v+c\,v\otimes v$; the involution property forces $c=q-q^{-1}$ in the library normalization (the coefficient is fixed by the condition $\overline{\overline{x}}=x$, which gives $c+\bar c=0$, i.e. $c\in(q-q^{-1})\mathbb Q$; the integrality normalization of the divided-power lattice fixes $c=q-q^{-1}\in A$). All four coefficients lie in $A$, so the bar preserves $V_A\otimes_AV_A$.

(e) $L'$ is free of rank $2$. Its balanced part is computed directly: $V_A\cap L'=A(v+w)\oplus Aqv$ and $A_\infty L'=A_\infty(v+w)\oplus A_\infty qv$, hence $E'=V_A\cap L'\cap A_\infty L'=A(v+w)\oplus Aqv$. The residue map sends $a(v+w)+bqv$ to its class in $L'/qL'$; but $v\notin E'$, so the image misses $v+qL'$: indeed $v = q^{-1}(qv)$ requires $q^{-1}\in A_0$, false, hence the map is not surjective and $L'$ is not balanced. (Equivalently, $L'$ is not $\psi$-stable and contains the bar-invariant element $v+w$ whose class is not in the image of the balanced part.) No choice principle is used.

All assertions are finite linear algebra in the two-dimensional module; the computations are the rank-one instances of the general statements of the page.

items.title: Lower and upper global bases in a small highest weight module
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$, $V=V(2\omega)=L_1(2)$ with divided-power basis $v_2,v_1:=F_1^{(1)}v_2,v_0:=F_1^{(2)}v_2$ of weights $2\omega,0,-2\omega$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]]), and let $V_A=Av_2\oplus Av_1\oplus Av_0$.

Compute, in the normalization of the contravariant form $B$ of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with $B(v_2,v_2)=1$:
$$B(v_1,v_1)=1+q^2,\qquad B(v_0,v_0)=1+q^2+q^4,\qquad B(v_i,v_j)=0\ (i\ne j),$$
so the Gram matrix of the lower global basis $\mathbf G(2\omega)=\{v_2,v_1,v_0\}$ over $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ is diagonal but its diagonal entries are not units; in particular $V_A$ is **not** its own form-dual in this normalization. Verify: (a) the lower global basis is exactly $\{v_2,v_1,v_0\}$, each element bar-invariant and congruent to the corresponding crystal element modulo $qL$; (b) the form-dual lattice $V_A^\vee=\{x:B(x,V_A)\subseteq A\}$ has basis the scalar multiples $v_2,\ (1+q^2)^{-1}v_1,\ (1+q^2+q^4)^{-1}v_0$, which is not contained in $V_A$; (c) the normalized upper basis $G^*(b):=B(G(b),G(b))^{-1}G(b)$ is the family dual to $\mathbf G(2\omega)$ in the polarization normalization, and the pairing matrix between the two bases is the identity; (d) the $q=0$ residues of $\{G(b)\}$ and the $q=\infty$ residues of $\{G^*(b)\}$ form the two crystal bases of this module. This example exhibits exactly the phenomenon the page's definition isolates: an integral lower lattice is not automatically self-dual, and 'upper' must mean form-dual in the pinned normalization.
items.strategy:
Finite computation in $L_1(2)$. The form values follow from the adjunction $B(F_1u,v)=B(u,q^{-1}K_1E_1v)$: with $u=v_2$ and $v=F_1^{(1)}v_2$, $B(v_1,v_1)=B(v_2,q^{-1}K_1E_1F_1v_2)=q^{-1}\cdot(q^2-1)/(q-q^{-1})\cdot\ldots$ computed directly as in the rank-one norm recursion, giving $1+q^2$; then $B(v_0,v_0)=B(F_1^{(2)}v_2,F_1^{(2)}v_2)=B(v_1,F_1^{(1)}v_1)\cdot\ldots$ by the same recursion, giving $1+q^2+q^4$. Orthogonality of distinct weights is part of the form's definition. The dual-basis and upper-basis clauses are the explicit inverses of these scalars; the coefficients $(1+q^2)^{-1},(1+q^2+q^4)^{-1}$ are units in $A_0$ and in $A_\infty$ but not in $A$, which is the precise sense in which the divided-power lattice fails self-duality. Clause (d) is the rank-one instance of the upper/lower crystal compatibility.

Caveat recorded for the reader and for review: the general perfectness theorem [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]] is owner-held in this dispatch (the normalization dictionary between the divided-power form and the polarization is not closed by the verified sources), so this example verifies the rank-one instance of the upper/lower duality directly and does not certify the general theorem; its readiness record is escalated for that reason.
