items.title: Matching the canonical and lower global normalizations in rank one and $A_2$
items.statement:
Check the dictionary of [[thm-lusztig-canonical-and-kashiwara-global-bases-agree-in-symmetric-type]] on two explicit cases.

(a) **Rank one.** For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$: (i) the divided powers $F_1^{(n)}$ are $\psi$-invariant and satisfy $F_1^{(n)}\equiv b_n\bmod qL(\infty)$ for the crystal elements $b_n$; (ii) they are the unique elements of $U_A^-\cap L(\infty)$ with these two properties; (iii) the form values are $(F_1^{(n)},F_1^{(n)})=q^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_1!$, so the generator normalization is the divided-power one and not the shuffle one; (iv) consequently the lower global basis of $U_q^-(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ is $\{F_1^{(n)}\}_{n\ge0}$, and any construction of the canonical basis in rank one that is normalized by $\psi$-invariance, the crystal congruence and the divided-power integral form produces the same family. The two remaining normalization choices are exhibited: using $F_1^n$ instead of $F_1^{(n)}$ multiplies the basis elements by the non-units $[n]_1!$, and using the shuffle form $(E_1,F_1)=(q-q^{-1})^{-1}$ instead of $(E_1,F_1)=1$ rescales the dual basis.

(b) **Type $A_2$, the two lowest mixed degrees.** With $A_2$ data $a_{12}=a_{21}=-1$, $q_1=q_2=q$: in degree $\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ the negative half has $\mathbb Q(q)$-basis $\{F_1F_2,F_2F_1\}$; both monomials are $\psi$-invariant, and the two crystal elements satisfy $b_i\equiv F_i\bmod qL(\infty)$, so the two lower global basis elements are $F_1F_2$ and $F_2F_1$ up to the triangular correction forced by the polarization; the example computes the correction explicitly in the divided-power normalization and verifies that the resulting basis is unitriangular with diagonal $1$ over $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. In degree $2\alpha_1$ the basis element is $F_1^{(2)}$.

This example is a normalization exhibit; it does not prove the general symmetric-type comparison, which is [[thm-lusztig-canonical-and-kashiwara-global-bases-agree-in-symmetric-type]] and is owner-held in this dispatch.
items.strategy:
Rank one: (i) is immediate from $\psi(F_1)=F_1$ and the definition of the crystal basis of $U_q^-(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ ([[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]] for the rank-one module and string formulas; the negative-half crystal is computed in the companion example of the crystal page). (ii) Uniqueness is the rank-one instance of [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]. (iii) is the explicit norm recursion $(F_1^{(n)},F_1^{(n)})=q^{-n(n-1)/2}/[n]_1!$ recorded in the form theorem; it shows the divided-power normalization. (iv) follows.

Type $A_2$: write the two monomials $F_1F_2$ and $F_2F_1$; the bar fixes both; the crystal elements are the two $\tilde f$-monomials of the unit; the polarization form in the divided-power basis has Gram matrix $\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&u\end{pmatrix}$ with $u,v\in A$ and $u\equiv1\bmod q$; the global basis is obtained by the unitriangular change of basis that makes the two basis vectors $\psi$-invariant and orthonormal modulo $q$; the computation is finite and all coefficients lie in $A$. The correction is the $A_2$ instance of the unitriangular expansion of the tensor/triangularity statements; the example records the exact matrix.

Caveat: the general comparison needs the full dictionary of [[thm-lusztig-canonical-and-kashiwara-global-bases-agree-in-symmetric-type]] and its owner-held source verification; the example certifies only the displayed finite cases.

items.title: Bar invariance and the congruence modulo $q$ do not imply balancedness
items.strategy:
Direct computation, with the basis computations of [[ex-balanced-triple-for-the-two-dimensional-quantum-sl-two-module]]. Clause (a): $v+w$ and $qv$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-independent, so $L'$ is free of rank $2$; $v=q^{-1}(qv)$ and $w=(v+w)-v$ show that $L'$ generates $V(\omega)$; $\tilde e_1(v+w)=\tilde e_1v+\tilde e_1w=0+v=v$, and $v=a(v+w)+bqv$ with $a,b\in A_0$ forces $a=0$ and $1=bq$, i.e. $b=q^{-1}\notin A_0$, so $v\notin L'$; finally the weight pieces are $L'_{\omega}=A_0qv$ and $L'_{\omega-\alpha_1}=qA_0w$, and $v+w=aqv+bqw$ forces $1=aq$, impossible in $A_0$, so $L'$ is not weight-decomposed.

(b) $v+w$ is fixed by $\psi$ because both $v$ and $w$ are, and it lies in $L'$, so $v+w\equiv v+w\bmod qL'$ trivially; this is exactly the normalization a global basis element must satisfy, and it shows that bar-invariance plus the congruence alone carry no basis information.

(c) $V_A(\omega)=Av\oplus Aw$; intersecting with $L'=A_0(v+w)\oplus A_0qv$ gives $E'=A(v+w)\oplus Aqv$ (an element $a(v+w)+bqv$ with $a,b\in A$ lies in $V_A$ and in $A_\infty L'$ because $q\in A_\infty^\times$); the residue classes of $v+w$ and $qv$ span a proper subgroup of $L'/qL'$: $v=q^{-1}(qv)$ requires $q^{-1}\in A_0$, which fails, so $L'=A_0(v+w)+A_0qv$ contains $v$ only as an $A_0$-combination with a $q^{-1}$ coefficient, and the class of $v$ is not in $\varphi(E')$. Hence the globalization map is not surjective, and $L'$ is not balanced.

(d) is the summary. No choice principle is used.
